How to search, inspect and compare the records

Use the Evidence hub to find a claim, indicator, visual or source-backed record, then inspect the definition, group covered, calculation base, period, geography, method, limitations, source and evidence date. Compare records when similar labels may hide different units or populations. Disagreement, series breaks and missing evidence remain visible rather than being averaged or filled in. The hub is an index for verification; detailed evidence lives in the linked records and comparison view.

Start here: selected evidence records

When was it measured or observed?The official 2026 roster (issue date not stated); 2026 enforcement decisions are separate evidence.
The official 2026 exchange and remittance roster can be counted; whether providers operate now is a separate question
The official 2026 roster of exchange and remittance providers issued by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) lists 100 exchange companies, 231 individual exchange establishments and 111 remittance agents. These are roster entries counted by the roster's own classes: the three class totals are not a count of unique providers, nor a verified count of providers operating now. Because the roster does not state its issue date, CBY-Aden's 2026 decisions (dated January to September 2026) suspending or withdrawing the licences of named entities, or closing their premises, would have to be matched with the roster entity by entity, since a decision may or may not already be reflected in it; that matching has not been done.
Who or what does it apply to? Source-listed exchange companies, individual exchange establishments and remittance agents; entries are counted separately by the three classes used in the official roster.
Does not establish: Adding the three classes does not give a count of unique providers, because no rule for identifying the same entity across classes has been applied. Inclusion in the annual roster is not proof of current operation, branch activity or service availability, including for entities named in 2026 enforcement decisions. Why the numbers differ: the 2025 roster (record CLM-016) listed fewer entries in each of its three classes. The higher 2026 entries cannot be read as new providers entering the market: both rosters count entries by class rather than unique firms, this evidence base has not compared the two rosters entry by entry, and the 2026 roster states no issue date.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-009
When was it measured or observed?Evidence observed from 2014 through 2026, depending on domain, as compared in the current edition of this resource.
Evidence freshness differs by domain
The evidence here is not equally current across domains: several payments/regulatory observations are from 2025–2026, while key representative people-side evidence is older.
Who or what does it apply to? Evidence records across people, payments, providers, reforms and other domains, each with its own observation period and evidence class.
Does not establish: Older evidence is not invalid because of its age, and recent administrative evidence does not measure current financial inclusion across the population.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-014
When was it measured or observed?Decisions dated 1 January to 24 September 2026
Enforcement decisions are events, not a market census
Governor's decisions of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) dated January to September 2026 record licence withdrawals, suspensions and closures for specific exchange and remittance providers. This record covers selected CBY-Aden Governor's decisions of 2026 concerning exchange and remittance providers (Nos. 1–6, 9–11, 13–15, 17 and 18); other decision numbers are not included and their subjects are not assessed. The official 2026 roster can be counted by class, but these decisions are not subtracted from it to produce a count of providers operating now: each would first have to be matched with the roster entity by entity, and that matching has not been done.
Who or what does it apply to? Only the providers named in the decisions covered here; not the full set of exchange and remittance providers
Does not establish: The 2026 annual roster can be counted by class, but it is not a census of operating providers. Subtracting suspension, withdrawal and closure decisions from the roster does not give a current count of operating providers: the roster does not state its issue date, so each entity a decision names would have to be matched with the roster one by one, without assuming whether the roster already reflects the decision, and that matching has not been done. A provider not named in these decisions is not thereby shown to be active or compliant. The record does not cover 2026 decision numbers other than those listed, and it does not assess their subjects.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-019
When was it measured or observed?World Bank variable pages for the Global Findex 2021 Yemen microdata; Yemen fieldwork 2022–2023.
Raw case shares are not population estimates
World Bank variable pages expose raw sample case counts and percentages for the Yemen Findex file, but explicitly warn that those figures cannot be interpreted as summary statistics of the population of interest.
Who or what does it apply to? Raw respondent cases displayed on World Bank variable pages; these are unweighted sample cases, not the population of Yemen.
Does not establish: The raw, unweighted case percentages shown on the World Bank variable pages are not estimates for Yemen's adult population and are not reported in this resource.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-024
When was it measured or observed?Function-specific people-side evidence: World Bank published values from the Findex 2021 wave (Yemen fieldwork 2022–2023) for most functions, and the 2014 country profile for historical detail.
There is no single latest year for all people-side evidence
The people-side evidence here does not have one latest year. The 2021 Findex wave (World Bank Data year 2022) gives World Bank published values for account ownership, saving, borrowing, digital payments, payments received, domestic remittances and emergency funds within 30 days; the 2014 country profile gives the historical detail shown here on how adults borrowed, saved and received domestic remittances in 2014; and the World Bank publishes no Yemen value for the reasons for not having an account. The 2014 and 2021-wave results stay separate and are not read as a trend.
Who or what does it apply to? People-side evidence by financial function; each function keeps its own survey wave, population base, denominator and publication status.
Does not establish: The 2014 behaviour values do not describe current behaviour, and raw case percentages from the 2021 wave are not a substitute for weighted population estimates.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-031
When was it measured or observed?World Development Indicators as checked on 11 October 2026; Migration and Development Brief 40 (June 2024)
A public interface is not the same thing as the underlying dataset
World Development Indicators holds no Yemen observation of personal remittances received after 2016 (last: USD 3,770.6 million in 2016; checked 11 October 2026). What one public interface holds is not evidence that later underlying data are absent. One World Bank publication is also inconsistent on Yemen: the note to Figure A.4.2 of Migration and Development Brief 40 (June 2024) says Yemen is excluded “due to data availability”, yet panel (a), remittances in US dollars for 2023, shows a value for Yemen, and only panel (b), remittances as a share of GDP, omits it. The brief does not say which panel the note applies to, and this resource takes no value from the figure.
Who or what does it apply to? Specific to each source or display interface
Does not establish: What one interface holds does not show that data were deleted or withdrawn, or why any correction was made, and one public interface's observations are not a substitute for another's.
Open evidence record Reference CLM-039
